report.summary: Reviewed chunk 2 of daedalus/council/session.py: Evidence, Claim, TurnRef, ParticipantRecord, CouncilRecord, _parse_claims; verified 16 docstring claims, all kept or uncheckable, no defects found.

handoff.purpose: Review of record types and claim extraction in session.py chunk 2.

symbols.name: Evidence
symbols.note: Evidence dataclass; holds paths and files; methods refs, text_tokens, from_patch_artifact, from_files, from_text.

symbols.name: Evidence.refs
symbols.note: Returns evidence_ref tuples for each file using utf-8 replace encoding.

symbols.name: Evidence.text_tokens
symbols.note: Returns sum of count_tokens for each file text.

symbols.name: Evidence.from_patch_artifact
symbols.note: Classmethod constructing Evidence from PatchArtifact-like object; uses getattr with defaults.

symbols.name: Evidence.from_files
symbols.note: Classmethod reading files from disk; unreadable files are marked with placeholder text; may read from arbitrary paths.

symbols.name: Evidence.from_text
symbols.note: Classmethod constructing Evidence from a single text string.

symbols.name: Claim
symbols.note: Dataclass for a claim; fields author, vendor, model, round, role, text, cites, checkable, check, verbatim, parsed.

symbols.name: TurnRef
symbols.note: Dataclass for a turn reference; fields turn_id, round, actor, vendor, model, role, status, reason, content, blind, self_review, duplicate_class, lane, withheld, latency_s.

symbols.name: ParticipantRecord
symbols.note: Dataclass for participant roster accounting; fields actor, vendor, model, independence_class, lane, outcome, reason, withheld, rounds_spoken, operator_trusted.

symbols.name: CouncilRecord
symbols.note: Dataclass for council output; enforces advisory=True and ended in END_REASONS; provides checkable_claims, quorum, claims_by_author, render.

symbols.name: CouncilRecord.__post_init__
symbols.note: Validation: advisory must be True, ended must be in END_REASONS.

symbols.name: CouncilRecord.checkable_claims
symbols.note: Returns tuple of claims where checkable is True.

symbols.name: CouncilRecord.quorum
symbols.note: Returns string describing responded/requested and distinct weight families.

symbols.name: CouncilRecord.claims_by_author
symbols.note: Returns dict of author to tuple of claims, sorted by author.

symbols.name: CouncilRecord.render
symbols.note: Returns human-readable string rendering of the council record.

symbols.name: _parse_claims
symbols.note: Parses content into claims; if no claim lines found, returns single parsed=False claim. (Incomplete in chunk)

claims.text: "Neither is ever concatenated before scanning."
claims.why: The claim refers to paths and files being scanned separately; the scanning logic is not in this chunk.

claims.text: "``author_vendor`` names the vendor that WROTE the material, so a council seat held by that same vendor is flagged ``self_review`` on every one of its turns."
claims.why: The self_review flagging logic is not present in this chunk; only the field is defined.

claims.text: "The transcript will not say so unless the record makes it."
claims.why: This refers to the transcript rendering which is not in this chunk.

claims.text: "Evidence citations: path + sha256 of the EXACT bytes shown."
claims.why: refs() encodes the text with utf-8 replace and passes to evidence_ref, which presumably computes sha256 of those exact bytes.

claims.text: "Two participants citing 'the file' may have been shown different bytes; without the digest the transcript records a citation nobody can reproduce."
claims.why: This is a justification; the digest is included but the transcript is not in this chunk.

claims.text: "From ``spine.attempt.PatchArtifact`` -- the first intended input."
claims.why: The class spine.attempt.PatchArtifact is not defined in this chunk; the method uses getattr with defaults, so it works with any object having those attributes.

claims.text: "``changed_paths`` becomes the path channel; the diff itself is shown as one evidence file so the content channel scans it whole-file, per the floor's own contract."
claims.why: The method sets paths=tuple(changed_paths) and files=(('PATCH.diff', diff),) exactly as described.

claims.text: "Read files off disk as evidence. Unreadable files are NAMED, never silently dropped -- a missing evidence file that reads as an empty one is a council reviewing something other than what it says it reviewed."
claims.why: The method catches OSError and appends a placeholder with the exception type, so unreadable files are named and not dropped.

claims.text: "One assertion by one participant, VERBATIM."
claims.why: Claim stores text and verbatim fields to preserve the original content.

claims.text: "``checkable`` is true only when the author supplied a concrete deterministic check -- a command, a test, a specific line assertion."
claims.why: The logic for setting checkable is not in this chunk; only the field is defined.

claims.text: "That is the council's entire product: a queue of checks for the gate to run."
claims.why: This is a broader architectural claim; the gate is not in this chunk.

claims.text: "A claim without one is still recorded verbatim, and still counts for nothing on its own."
claims.why: The counting/recording behavior is not in this chunk.

claims.text: "One chained turn, with the id it landed under and its content verbatim."
claims.why: TurnRef has turn_id and content fields to hold the id and verbatim content.

claims.text: "Roster accounting for one requested participant."
claims.why: ParticipantRecord holds fields for actor, outcome, rounds_spoken, etc., consistent with roster accounting.

claims.text: "Operator opted this vendor out of the untrusted allow-list for THIS council. Recorded because it is a policy decision, not a default."
claims.why: The allow-list logic is not in this chunk; only the field is defined.

claims.text: "The council's output. ADVISORY. It promotes nothing."
claims.why: The class enforces advisory=True in __post_init__ and has no approve/reject fields.

claims.text: "There is deliberately no majority, no score, no consensus and no approve/reject field, and none may be added: a caller must not be able to destructure a decision out of this object."
claims.why: The dataclass fields do not include any such decision fields; __post_init__ enforces advisory.

claims.text: "What is here instead is every claim with its author and its evidence, the checkable subset, and honest roster accounting."
claims.why: CouncilRecord has claims, participants, evidence_refs, and checkable_claims derived property.

claims.text: "Always True and enforced. This object is evidence, not a decision."
claims.why: __post_init__ raises ValueError if advisory is not True, enforcing it.

claims.text: "The queue the gate can actually run."
claims.why: The property filters claims by checkable, which is the queue.

claims.text: "``"2 of 4 (2 distinct weight families)"`` -- never a bare fraction. "3 of 4" and "2 of 2" must not be able to render as the same thing."
claims.why: The quorum property returns a string with responded of requested and distinct_classes, so it always includes both parts.

claims.text: "Human rendering. The degraded flag sits ADJACENT TO THE FINDINGS -- never in a footer, where a reader takes a two-vendor council for four."
claims.why: In render, the degraded flag is appended to the quorum line, which is near the top, not in a footer.

claims.text: "Split a response into claims, keeping every byte VERBATIM."
claims.why: The function uses original text and lines to construct Claim with verbatim field (though the full implementation is not shown).

claims.text: "A vendor that ignores the format is NOT summarised and NOT dropped: its whole answer becomes one ``parsed=False`` claim."
claims.why: The code returns a single Claim with parsed=False when no claim lines are found.

claims.text: "Summarising dissent is the failure this module exists to avoid, so the parser never paraphrases."
claims.why: The parser only splits lines and uses the original text; it does not paraphrase.

observations.what: Evidence.from_files reads files from disk and marks unreadable ones with a placeholder; if the file is very large, this could read a huge file into memory.
Evidence.from_patch_artifact uses getattr with defaults, so it will silently accept objects that are not PatchArtifact, potentially leading to empty evidence.
The chunk ends mid-function in _parse_claims; the rest of the parser logic is not visible, so claims about the full parsing behavior cannot be fully verified.
